description.p: Sealwax is a fast, minimal email client, quick to drive from the keyboard and careful with every message: no script in a message ever runs, and nothing from the internet loads until you allow it.

ul.li: Accounts without server settings: type your address and Sealwax finds the servers; Sign in with Microsoft for Outlook.com and Microsoft 365, app passwords for others
IMAP with push and an offline copy of your mail, and POP3 into local folders
Whole conversations, safe HTML, attachments that open safely and link warnings
Archive, delete, move, star and mark many messages at once, with Undo, also offline
Folders, and rules in Sieve, the standard mail-filter language, made in a dialog
A rich-text composer, drafts kept on the server and an outbox with Undo send
Search with from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment and more, with suggestions as you type
Unsubscribe in one click, group mail by sender or domain, and pin the senders you mustn't miss
One-key shortcuts, a command palette and your own keys
Passwords only in your keyring, no telemetry, and logs without mail content

description.p: Sealwax follows the system's light or dark style. On Omarchy it also follows the live theme and Hyprland's rounded corners.
Help: the user guide is at pixdevs.com/guides/sealwax, and support answers at support@pixdevs.com. Contact Support… in Sealwax's main menu gives you the address and the details that help.

description.p: Empty Trash: an account's Trash folder has Empty Trash on its sidebar menu, which deletes the folder's messages for good, on the server too, including older mail Sealwax never downloaded. Undo in the toast stands for the usual seven seconds.

Help, also without a GitHub account: the main menu's Help submenu has User Guide, which opens the online guide, Contact Support…, which shows the support address with the details that help and can start the message, Report an Issue and About Sealwax. The setup assistant offers the same help when an account can't be added.

The message list can be shown on its own, without the reading pane: Toggle Reading Pane in the main menu makes a message open in the list's place, in a window of any width. The keyboard stays in the list when the window changes width, and one folder a mail server won't report on no longer hides an account's other folders.

Sealwax as a Flatpak, for Linux systems other than Omarchy, from Sealwax's own Flatpak repository, with updates through Flatpak. Software centres can now describe Sealwax, and a network monitor that first says there is no network no longer makes every account reconnect at start.
A security update: a mail server can no longer keep Sealwax busy with one long reply.
Folders with a backslash or a quote in their name sync.
The message list keeps its place when rows change under the selection.
